\vspace{2pt}
\begin{minipage}{\textwidth}\footnotesize
One engine per row, placed and routed alone on XC7S75-1 at 50\,MHz. Operands come from on-chip xorshift64 generators (identical in every build); each engine accumulates 64-word vectors, and every accumulator is XOR-reduced to an output pin so that no logic is pruned. LUT, FF and power are net of a stimulus-only build. Act. $\times$ weight: operand widths. \\
$^{*}$Engine dynamic power: \texttt{report\_power} (post-route, vectorless default switching) of the build minus that of the stimulus-only build. Comparable across rows; not a measurement on silicon. \\
$^{\dagger}$Scaled to the same throughput, 32 terms/cycle (= 1.58 G terms/s with one start cycle per 64-word vector). Per-term energy = this power $/$ term rate: 1.19, 15.2, 27.3, 38.7\,pJ for rows 2--5. Table IV uses rows 2--4. \\
$^{\P}$\texttt{report\_power} prints 1\,mW steps ($\pm$17\% at 3\,mW), so the binary reference is the 8-engine build. Shared control logic makes it 88 LUT per engine against 173 alone; the real design, with one engine per layer, is the latter.
\end{minipage}
